+title: Open spans for session creation and session restore
+---
+## What
+
+"Session" is one of the named surfaces to cover, but the tracing set has no span for how a session comes into being. Add one. The restore path is the one that earns it most: it reads a transcript tree from disk and rebuilds state, so its cost is real and invisible today.
+
+- Instrument the shared factory `makeRoutedSessionActor` (Sources/FoundationModelsRouter/Session/RoutedSessionActor.swift:8, constructing at line 40), so all three construction sites are covered at once: `RoutedLLM.swift:156` (a new session), `Recording/SessionTreeRestoration.swift:368` (a restored session), and `Session/RoutedSessionActorForking.swift:158` (a forked child).
+- Span name: `FoundationModelsRouter.session` from `RouterTracing`. Kind: `.internal`.
+- Attributes: `router.id`, `model.ref`, the new `session.id`, the parent `session.id` when there is one, and the origin (`new`, `restored`, or `forked`).
+- A forked child therefore carries both a `FoundationModelsRouter.fork` span and a `FoundationModelsRouter.session` span. The fork span measures the wait for a slot; the session span measures the construction. Nest the session span inside the fork span, and state this in the doc comment so the pair does not read as double counting.
+- For the restore path, put the span around the tree read and the rebuild, not only the actor construction, so the disk work lands inside it.
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+- [ ] Making a session, restoring a session, and forking a session each produce one `FoundationModelsRouter.session` span with the matching origin attribute.
+- [ ] A forked child's session span is nested inside its fork span.
+- [ ] A restored session's span covers the transcript-tree read.
+
+## Tests
+- [ ] Add `Tests/FoundationModelsRouterTests/SessionCreationTracingTests.swift`. Use `InMemoryTracer` with the fixtures from `SessionTreeRestorationTests.swift` and `ForkConcurrencyTests.swift`.
+- [ ] Assert the span name, the three origin values, the attributes, and the fork/session nesting.
+- [ ] Run `swift test`. All tests pass.
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — write failing tests first, then implement to make them pass. #tracing #router
\ No newline at end of file

+    Picked up. Research notes:
+
+    - The shared factory `makeRoutedSessionActor` (Sources/FoundationModelsRouter/Session/RoutedSessionActor.swift) is synchronous, so its span must use the synchronous `withSpan` overload. `RoutedLLM.makeSession` is a public synchronous API, so the factory cannot become async.
+    - `RouterTracing.SpanName.session` and the two `tool` markers are the only `// periphery:ignore` markers in the tracing vocabulary. This card removes the `session` marker only.
+    - No parent-session attribute key exists yet. `AttributeKey.sessionId` ("session.id") and `AttributeKey.forkChildSessionId` ("fork.child_session_id") are the only session keys.
+    - Fork nesting comes free: `withForkSpan` runs `performFork` inside `ServiceContext.$current.withValue(...)`, and the task-local survives the actor hop, so a span opened by the factory inside that body records the fork span as its parent. `InMemoryTracer` reads the parent from the context, and `FinishedInMemorySpan` exposes `spanID`/`parentSpanID`, so the nesting is assertable.
+    - Restore disk work: `TranscriptTree.load(under:)` reads every `session.json`, once for the whole tree. `tree.effectiveTranscript(forSession:)` and `tree.effectiveEntryEvents(forSession:)` re-read `transcript.jsonl` from disk for the node AND for each ancestor (TranscriptTree.decodeEvents). So a per-node span that starts before those two calls really does cover the transcript-tree read.
+    - Test-suite audit for unfiltered span counting: only ResolveTracingTests reads `tracer.finishedSpans.count` unfiltered, and that test resolves a profile without making a session, so the new span cannot reach it. EmbedTracingTests, TurnTracingTests, CompactionTracingTests and ForkTracingTests all filter by operation name; SessionTracerWiringTests uses `contains`. No existing assertion needs weakening.
+    - SpanContentSafetyTests reads every attribute of every span and names none, so it measures the new span with no edit.

+- actor: claude-code
+  id: 01m14ppte6h2pwqm1c31h7s4np
+  text: |-
+    Implementation landed, TDD order kept: the new suite was written first and all three tests failed with "0 session spans" before any source change.
+
+    Design note, because one part of the card needed a decision. The card asks for two things that pull apart: instrument the one shared factory, AND make the restore span cover the tree read that happens BEFORE the factory can be called. The answer:
+
+    - `describeSession(on:origin:routerId:sessionId:parentId:model:)` in RoutedSessionActor.swift writes the name's attributes, and it is the only writer for all three shapes.
+    - `makeRoutedSessionActor` gains a required `origin:` parameter (no default, for the same reason `tracer` has none) and opens the span around the construction for `new` and `forked`.
+    - `withRestoredSessionSpan(routerId:sessionId:parentId:model:tracer:_:)` opens the same span for the restore path, around the read and the rebuild together, and the factory opens no second span for `origin == .restored`. Both paths use the same span name, the same kind and the same one attribute writer.
+
+    Restore restructuring: the per-node work moved out of `restore(_:)` into a new nested `rebuild(_:on:)`, so the span closure holds `effectiveTranscript`, `effectiveEntryEvents`, the backend build and the construction. The child recursion stayed in `restore(_:)`, outside the span, so a parent's span measures only its own node and never its whole subtree.
+
+    Fork nesting needed no wiring: the fork span's `ServiceContext` task-local reaches the factory through the actor hop, so the session span records the fork span as its parent. The test asserts `span.parentSpanID == forkSpan.spanContext.spanID`.
+
+    `// periphery:ignore` removed from `SpanName.session`. The two `tool` markers stay, that card has not landed. Two keys added to `RouterTracing.AttributeKey` rather than literals: `session.parent_id` and `session.origin`, plus the `RouterTracing.SessionOrigin` enum beside `TurnEntryPoint` and `CompactionTrigger`.
+
+    No existing test needed a change. The audit found only ResolveTracingTests counting `finishedSpans` unfiltered, and that test makes no session.
